top_categories.workout_context: 123ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
16,597ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
At mile 60 of 135, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 135 miles.
16,597ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti. Train it until it feels boring.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 135 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 16,597ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 16,597ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.weather: June in Lienz, East Tyrol, Austria. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti’s 135 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Dolomitenradrundfahrt / SuperGiroDolomiti rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.
